correctness.rationale: For n>=3, B=2^n, A=7B, m=A+1 and S=<A2^i+1>, the residues mod m are represented by w(t)=At+m*lambda(t) for 0<=t<=A, where lambda minimizes number of Mersenne coins (2^j-1). Nonnegative combination normalization plus lambda(t)<=t handles all multiples of m. The Apéry gap p(t)=w(t)-m is pseudo-Frobenius if each nonwrapping added coin c_j satisfies lambda(t+c_j)<=lambda(t); wrapping additions are automatically in S. Binary digit sum gives exact lambda(B-d)=d, lambda(A-d)=d (5<=d<=n+2), lambda(t1)=lambda(t2)=n+2 with t1=4B-n-2, t2=6B-n-2. Constructive coin decompositions bound all suffix values after t1 by n+2. Also lambda(A)=4,lambda(A-1)=5 and small suffix upper bounds, proving all displayed indices. Distinct residues give exactly n+2 explicit PF elements and type>=n+2, not exact type. Independent Dijkstra/coin checks verified n=3,4,5,6 and all proposed gaps, not an all-n proof.
